title: China startup demoes prototype EUV light source — 15W of output power and 90% domestic components, still years away from viability
key_facts: Chinese start-up Langdao Silex demonstrated a prototype EUV light source this week at the 26th China International Industry Fair in Shanghai, without lighting it.
Claims: over 15 W of EUV output, 90 percent domestic components, over 100 hours of continuous running; no way to verify them.
Langdao was set up in 2024 by alumni of Tsinghua University's Gas Discharge Plasma Laboratory.
TrendForce, citing various sources, says it needs three to five more years to commercialise.
Tom's Hardware notes the 15 W may be measured at the plasma, not at the intermediate focus used by ASML, so usable power would be lower.
A full EUV scanner also needs collection and illumination optics, multilayer mirrors, wafer and reticle stages and a supply chain that hardly exists in China today.
Tom's Hardware concludes China has not got significantly closer to its own EUV scanner.
quote_evidence: This week, Chinese startup Langdao Silex demonstrated a prototype extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light source with over 15W of output power, 90% domestic components, and decent uptime.
The company will need another three to five years to commercialize its technology, reports TrendForce, citing various sources.
Langdao Silex has not demonstrated its EUV light source in action, so all we know about it comes from the company itself.
why_it_matters_hint: China is trying to build the EUV technology it cannot buy from ASML, but this is an unverified prototype light source only.
event_date: this week (fair in Shanghai); exact day not stated
notes: Tom's Hardware's own analysis built on a TrendForce report; TrendForce original not read.
